title: From stored energy to moving wheels
description: A schematic side view of a rear-wheel-drive electric car. Select a numbered part or follow the energy route. The front of the car is on the right; component positions and proportions are simplified.

regions.label: Body and cabin
regions.description: The body encloses the passenger space. Its silhouette is separate from the underfloor power system in this diagram.

regions.label: Traction battery
regions.description: Stores energy. The flat gold pack is shown below the passenger cabin, between the axles.

regions.label: Power electronics
regions.description: Controls electrical power supplied to the motor. The diagram separates it from the motor so the connection is easier to follow.

regions.label: Traction motor
regions.description: Converts electrical energy into mechanical rotation. A reduction gear transfers torque to the driven wheels.

regions.label: Driven wheels
regions.description: The rear wheels are driven in this example. The tyre-road contact transmits forces that accelerate or slow the vehicle.

flow.title: Follow the power path
flow.description: Gold and orange show an electrical path; blue shows mechanical power. The moving dot is a teaching cue, not an electron, a measured speed or a representation of electrical current direction.

steps.label: Battery → power electronics
steps.description: The traction battery supplies electrical energy to the power electronics.

steps.label: Power electronics → motor
steps.description: The controller regulates electrical power delivered to the traction motor.

steps.label: Motor → driven wheels
steps.description: The motor produces torque. Gearing and shafts transmit it to the rear wheels.

steps.label: Tyres → road
steps.description: Forces at the tyre-road contact accelerate the car. Real systems lose some energy as heat along the way.

poster.alt: Numbered car side view: 1 body, 2 battery, 3 power electronics, 4 motor and 5 driven rear wheels. Front is on the right.
